findings.claim_locator: FINAL_PROPOSAL.md line 154 (§7 B3 check 5), lines 149–156; initial PROPOSAL.md line 114
findings.finding: The written overlay gate permits labels without dataset coordinateTransformations to fall back to a shared grid from an informative equal-dimension-or-1 layout note. NGFF 0.4 requires coordinateTransformations on every datasets dictionary, including labels via required multiscales. The layout note supplies no transform or registration evidence. The fallback is both inconsistent with the strict missing-transform refusal elsewhere in the final plan and insufficient for the brief’s justify-or-withhold rule.
findings.diagnostic: Equal image/label shapes and equal level count plus image-label association, but absent label coordinateTransformations, is admitted by check5’s fallback without evidence of common origin, scale or units.
findings.quality_effect: Whole-case pass blocked even if all other claims were accurate.

findings.claim_locator: FINAL_PROPOSAL.md line 70 (napari supplies per-level world transforms), lines 164–165 (expose transforms + native auto/lock)
findings.finding: The pinned component’s public scale and translate are layer-wide. Native multiscale downsample factors are derived from shape ratios; tile translation comes from crop corners, not arbitrary NGFF per-level translations. The plan’s generic own interpretation layer does not specify the bridge required to render its own V1 declaration under native auto/lock mode. This is a gap in the research-to-plan applicability claim, not an assertion that no custom bridge could be built.
findings.diagnostic: For V1 with base scale0.5, base translation0, native shape ratio2 and full-level crop corner0, native default origin is0µm; NGFF level1 origin is+0.25µm.
findings.quality_effect: B2/B3 behavior remains unspecified for the required per-level offsets.

findings.finding: The five-check gate compares per-level scale/translation and axes order/length without requiring unit normalization or checking complete group-plus-dataset maps. Identical numeric transforms and shapes can represent different physical grids if image units are micrometer and label units nanometer. The plan gives no condition that prevents this case from reaching a shown overlay.
